Bug_Title: "@Controller" classes that use "@SessionAttributes" must call "setComplete" on their "SessionStatus" objects
Bug_Explanation: This is a simple bug in Spring MVC. A @Controller annotated class uses @SessionAttributes to store data on the server between requests. That data should be cleaned up when the session is over, but unless setComplete() is called on the SessionStatus object from a @RequestMapping method, neither Spring nor the JVM will know it’s time to do that. Note that the SessionStatus object must be passed to that method as a parameter.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case 'testBug' calls the greet() method and verifies the response. This does not trigger the bug because'setComplete' is not invoked on the SessionStatus object.
Model_Explanation: The provided Java code does not contain the described bug. The @Controller class HelloWorldController uses @SessionAttributes, but it does not call setComplete() on its SessionStatus object. However, the code does not violate the rule because it does not use @SessionAttributes. The rule is only applicable to @Controller classes that use @SessionAttributes.
